cards.text: Meet Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. The Moabites and Ammonites, together with some of the Meunites, come to make war against him. Three nations at once, friend, and he did NOT send out invitations.

cards.question: Some men come to warn Jehoshaphat that a vast army is coming against him. Where's it coming from?
That vast army is already on its way, and Jehoshaphat is alarmed. What does he do?

answers.text: He sets his face to seek the LORD
He calls up every soldier in Judah
He sends gold to buy them off

cards.question: To seek the LORD, Jehoshaphat proclaims a ___ throughout Judah.
When Jehoshaphat calls the people to seek the LORD, only the people of Jerusalem show up.

cards.text: Then Jehoshaphat stands in the assembly at the house of the LORD and prays. Before he says one word about the army, he says this: "O LORD, God of our fathers, are You not the God who is in heaven, and do You not rule over all the kingdoms of the nations?"

cards.question: Jehoshaphat reminds God that He gave this land forever to the descendants of ___, His friend.

cards.text: He reminds God what His people said when they built a sanctuary for His Name. If disaster ever comes, whether sword or judgment, plague or famine, they'll stand before this temple and cry out to Him.

cards.question: When God's people built the sanctuary, what did they say God would do when they cried out to Him in distress?

cards.text: Then he names the trouble: the men of Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir. When Israel came out of Egypt, God didn't let Israel invade them, so Israel turned away and left them alone.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat says Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir are repaying Judah by coming to make peace.

cards.text: Israel spared them, and now they're coming to drive Judah out of the land God gave as an inheritance. That's like letting a guy crash on your couch for a week, and he comes back to change the LOCKS.

Then the king says it right out loud: "For we are powerless before this vast army that comes against us." A KING said that, friend, in front of EVERYBODY. I can't even admit a batch is burnt, and I'm standing there holding the SMOKE.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat admits Judah is powerless against this vast army. What does he say next?

answers.text: They don't know what to do but their eyes are on God
They will fight on until the very last man falls
They will send to Egypt for horses and chariots

cards.question: While the king prays, the men of Judah are standing before the LORD with their wives, children and little ones.

cards.text: Then the Spirit of the LORD comes upon Jahaziel, a Levite from Asaph's descendants, right there in the assembly. He calls out, "Listen, all you people of Judah and Jerusalem! Listen, King Jehoshaphat!"

cards.question: Jahaziel says this is what the LORD says: don't be afraid of this vast army, because the battle does not belong to Judah but to ___.

cards.text: Tomorrow they march down, and they'll find the army coming up the Ascent of Ziz, at the end of the valley facing the Wilderness of Jeruel. Friend, that's more detail than a location PIN.

cards.question: God tells Judah to go out and face the vast army tomorrow. What does He say their part in the battle is?

answers.text: Stand firm and see the LORD save them
Fight hard and drive the army back
Surround the camp and strike at night

cards.text: Jehoshaphat bows facedown, and all the people of Judah and Jerusalem fall down before the LORD to worship Him. Then the Levites from the Kohathites and Korahites stand up and praise the LORD, shouting in a very loud voice, and NOBODY is whispering in that assembly.
Early in the morning, they get up and head out for the Wilderness of Tekoa. No snooze button on THIS morning, friend, and as they set out, Jehoshaphat stands up to speak.

cards.question: As Judah sets out toward the vast army, what does Jehoshaphat tell the people to do?

answers.text: Believe in the LORD and His prophets
Keep their swords ready the whole way
Turn back if their hearts are afraid

cards.question: Jehoshaphat consults with the people and appoints some of them to go out in front of the army. Who are they?

cards.text: As they go out before the army, the singers sing: "Give thanks to the LORD, for His loving devotion endures forever." The choir is the FRONT LINE, friend, and the soldiers are the backup singers.

cards.question: The moment the singers begin their shouts and praises, what does the LORD do to the men of Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir?

answers.text: He sends hailstones down on them
He sends hornets out against them

cards.text: Then the Ammonites and Moabites rise up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir, devoting them to destruction. And Judah hasn't swung a single sword.

cards.question: Once Seir is finished off, the Ammonites and Moabites make peace with each other.
The men of Judah reach a place overlooking the wilderness and look for the vast army. What do they see?

answers.text: Only bodies lying on the ground
The army lined up for battle
An empty camp and fresh tracks

cards.text: Jehoshaphat and his people go to carry off the plunder, and they find goods and valuables, more than they could carry away. I can't carry two cookie boxes across my bakery without my mustache asking for a BREAK.

cards.question: There's so much plunder that Judah spends ___ days gathering it.
On the fourth day, Judah assembles in the Valley of Beracah and blesses the LORD there.

cards.text: That's why the place is called the Valley of Beracah to this day. Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem head back to Jerusalem with Jehoshaphat at their head, full of joy, because the LORD had made them rejoice over their enemies.

cards.question: When they get back to Jerusalem, they go into the house of the LORD with harps, lyres and trumpets.
When all the kingdoms of the lands hear that the LORD fought against Israel's enemies, the ___ of God comes upon them.

cards.text: Jehoshaphat's kingdom is at peace, because his God gave him rest on every side.
He became king at thirty-five and reigned in Jerusalem twenty-five years. He walked in the way of his father Asa and did what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
But the people had not yet set their hearts on the God of their fathers.

cards.question: With the people's hearts not yet set on the God of their fathers, the high places are all removed during Jehoshaphat's reign.

cards.text: Later, Jehoshaphat makes an alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly. Together they build ships in Ezion-geber to go to Tarshish.

cards.question: A prophet named Eliezer son of Dodavahu prophesies against Jehoshaphat for allying himself with Ahaziah. What happens to their ships?

answers.text: They're wrecked and can't sail to Tarshish
Ahaziah takes them all for himself
They're seized while still in port

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote line, "A KING said that, friend, in front of EVERYBODY." and "I can't even admit a batch is burnt, and I'm standing there holding the SMOKE." Only the opening card may run to three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The statement adds a time span, "during Jehoshaphat's reign," that 2 Chronicles 20:33 doesn't give. The verse only says the high places were not removed. Because 2 Chronicles 17:6 says Jehoshaphat removed the high places from Judah, a baker could argue that "True" is right.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Opening with "With the people's hearts not yet set on the God of their fathers" ties the two halves of 2 Chronicles 20:33 together as cause and result. The verse sets them side by side with a semicolon and leaves the connection open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Eliezer's actual words are never told: "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has destroyed your works" (2 Chronicles 20:37). The card only says the ships were wrecked. The baker never learns that the LORD is the one who destroyed Jehoshaphat's works, and that is the key point of the passage's final scene.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
